_source: From karandeep_contract_checklist.md, negotiation_notes.md and docs/Obligations_Register.md §G (fairness gate → precedent filter → approval). Seeded as approved on Karandeep's behalf for the prototype (declared in README). Precedents carry intent labels; exceptions/concessions are context, accidents are lessons, never precedent.

rules.standard: 0.5% of the affected milestone fee per week of delay attributable to AtliQ, capped at 5% of that milestone fee; no LDs for client-caused delay; LDs are the sole remedy for delay.
rules.acceptableRange: Weekly rate on the milestone (not total contract value) with a hard cap. Anything above 5% of the milestone is a deliberate exception only.
neverAccept: Uncapped LDs (checklist: "cap it. never open ended")
LDs per day, or calculated on total contract value
No exclusion for client-caused delay
LDs on top of actual damages, or carved out of the liability cap
rules.counterPosition: 0.5% of the affected milestone fee per week, capped at 5% of that milestone fee; no LDs where the delay is caused by the client; LDs are the sole and exclusive remedy for delay.

rules.standard: Invoices payable within 30 days of receipt; 45 days is the negotiated maximum.
neverAccept: More than 45 days
Pay-when-paid / pay-if-paid
Invoices waived if not submitted within a short window
Set-off across unrelated agreements
rules.counterPosition: Payment within 30 days of receipt of invoice (45 days maximum); no pay-when-paid; set-off limited to undisputed amounts under this agreement.

rules.standard: Each party's aggregate liability capped at 1× fees (paid or payable in the prior 12 months), mutual; carve-outs only for fraud, wilful misconduct and confidentiality (plus any carve-outs that are mandatory under the governing law, e.g. German law for intent/gross negligence and injury).
neverAccept: Unlimited liability for AtliQ ("1x fees. NOT unlimited")
A cap for one side only
LDs or data incidents carved out of the cap without limit
rules.counterPosition: Mutual cap of 1× fees paid or payable in the 12 months before the claim; carve-outs limited to fraud, wilful misconduct and breach of confidentiality; data-protection liability under a separate super-cap (e.g. 2× fees).

precedents.label: standard
precedents.note: Walked away from a €120k deal over unlimited liability (Jan 2026)

precedents.label: standard
precedents.note: AtliQ-friendly master: capped liability

precedents.label: standard
precedents.note: Counsel-reviewed: BAA liability capped at 2× trailing-12-month fees

precedents.label: accident
precedents.note: LDs carved out of the 150% cap

rules.standard: Mutual: each party covers its own breach and negligence; never the other side's negligence. IP-infringement indemnity for deliverables is normal.
neverAccept: Indemnifying the other party for its own negligence
One-way uncapped indemnity
Indemnity for 'any and all losses' regardless of fault
rules.counterPosition: Each party indemnifies the other for third-party claims caused by its own breach or negligence; no indemnity for losses caused by the indemnified party's own negligence; indemnities subject to the liability cap (IP infringement excepted).

precedents.label: standard
precedents.note: Origin: "we can't insure against PayTrack's own negligence" (Jan 2025)

precedents.label: standard
precedents.note: Mutual indemnity

rules.source: Checklist ("indemnity → mutual. we don't cover their mistakes"); negotiation notes (PayTrack)

rules.standard: The client owns what AtliQ builds specifically for it (on payment); AtliQ keeps its background IP, pre-existing tools and know-how and grants a licence to use them as part of the deliverables.
neverAccept: Assigning pre-existing tools / background IP (e.g. PipeKit)
Warranting sole ownership of tools AtliQ has already assigned elsewhere
IP vesting on creation before payment
rules.counterPosition: Client owns deliverables created specifically for it upon payment; AtliQ retains background IP and grants a non-exclusive, perpetual, royalty-free licence to use it as part of the deliverables.

precedents.label: standard
precedents.note: Client owns deliverables, AtliQ keeps background IP

precedents.label: accident
precedents.note: Pre-existing tools incl. PipeKit assigned to Northwind ("I skimmed the IP")

rules.source: Checklist ("IP → client owns what we build for them, we keep our own stuff")

rules.standard: Every freelancer / vendor assigns the work product to AtliQ (from creation or at least on payment) so AtliQ can give clients what it promises; their pre-existing tools are licensed broadly enough for the client deal.
neverAccept: Vendor keeps the work product and AtliQ only gets a non-exclusive or non-transferable licence while the client was promised ownership or exclusive rights
rules.counterPosition: Contractor assigns all rights in the work product to AtliQ; pre-existing materials are licensed on terms that let AtliQ pass to the client what the client contract requires.

precedents.label: accident
precedents.note: Rohan kept the Work Product while Acme was promised ownership ("ok" from phone)

rules.standard: Mutual in substance, not just in title: both parties' information protected, both bound by the same obligations, residuals mutual or none, mutual remedies, fixed term, and no non-competes or non-solicits hidden inside an NDA.
neverAccept: Confidential Information defined as only one party's information
One-way residuals clause
Non-compete / exclusivity inside an NDA
One-way uncapped indemnity
Perpetual one-way obligations
rules.counterPosition: Make the definitions and obligations mutual, delete residuals (or make them mutual), delete restrictive covenants, mutual remedies (injunction may be sought by either party), fixed 2–3 year term.

rules.standard: Indian law for AtliQ Technologies Pvt Ltd; US (state) law for AtliQ Inc; neutral or home forum.
rules.acceptableRange: The client's law has been accepted case by case to win a deal (DIFC, English, Singapore): a judgment call, not a blocker.
neverAccept: Foreign law on AtliQ Inc that nobody noticed (Brightwater)
rules.counterPosition: Laws of India (Pvt Ltd) / the relevant US state (Inc); arbitration seated in India or a neutral seat.

rules.standard: AtliQ Inc contracts with US clients only; AtliQ Technologies Pvt Ltd with everyone else. The contracting entity must equal the invoicing entity.
neverAccept: A non-US client contracting with AtliQ Inc
Parties clause and invoicing clause naming different AtliQ entities
rules.counterPosition: Name the correct AtliQ entity in the parties clause, invoicing clause and signature block.
rules.source: atliq_entities.md (finance): mismatches caused two payment delays in 2025

rules.standard: None, or narrow geography + short duration, always checked against the register; mutual exit where possible. No non-competes on freelancers/vendors beyond non-solicit of client staff.
neverAccept: Worldwide or open-ended non-competes
Client-capture clauses that take AtliQ's own relationships
Exclusivity without an exit
rules.counterPosition: Delete, or limit to named competitors in a defined territory for the term only, with a mutual termination right.

rules.standard: DPA (EU) or BAA (US health) signed before any personal/regulated data moves, with a sub-DPA / sub-BAA for every party that touches the data (incl. AtliQ's own Pune entity); engagement-specific scope; offshore access only as the agreement allows.
neverAccept: Data moving before the agreement exists
Subcontractors processing data without flowed-down terms and client consent
Uncapped liability for data incidents
rules.counterPosition: Execute the DPA/BAA and the sub-agreements first; agree a de-identified offshore route in writing; cap data-incident liability at a super-cap.

precedents.label: standard
precedents.note: Counsel-reviewed: capped liability, 5-day reporting, de-identified offshore route

rules.standard: On any termination for convenience AtliQ is paid for all work done, including work in progress. Notice is mutual. Client contracts: reasonable notice (typically 30+ days). Freelancer / vendor agreements: a mutual short exit (about 15 days, as with Rohan Iyer) is AtliQ's standard and fair to both sides.
neverAccept: Payment only for accepted deliverables on convenience termination
One-sided notice periods (e.g. 24 hours for AtliQ vs 60 days for the other side)
rules.counterPosition: Payment for all services performed up to termination, including work in progress and committed costs; mutual notice period.

precedents.label: standard
precedents.note: Mutual 15-day exit

rules.source: Checklist ("termination → they pay for work done")

rules.standard: Check every required insurance type and limit against what AtliQ actually holds before signing (known: cyber $1M; everything else unrecorded).
neverAccept: Committing to limits AtliQ doesn't hold, with certificates due before work starts
rules.counterPosition: Align required limits with current cover, or agree a timeline and cost to increase cover before signature.

rules.standard: Apply the same standard AtliQ asks for as a supplier: capped penalties or none, 30-day pay, mutual caps, no pay-when-paid, fair termination. Pass the client's obligations down (IP, confidentiality, data protection, consent), never the client's leverage.
neverAccept: Clauses AtliQ would reject from a client ("I don't want our paper to be the thing I hate receiving")
Missing flow-down of obligations promised to the end client
rules.counterPosition: Use the fair version of each clause and add back-to-back flow-down terms for the linked client contract.
